stops.note: 'ox-hide'; legend says Dido bought as much land at Carthage as one ox-hide could cover, cut it into thin strips, and named the citadel Byrsa
'purse', from the leather it was made of; also the source of English 'purse' and 'bursar'
reached Gaelic through Middle Irish sparán; worn at the front because the belted plaid had no pockets
Walter Scott staged George IV's 1822 visit to Edinburgh as a tartan pageant, with the king in full Highland dress, helping make the sporran part of formal kilt wear

current_meaning: a pouch worn at the front of a kilt
